headline_stat.name: median absolute decoding error, train square -> test triangle

stated_limitation: 91% of units are statistically significant at p < 0.01, which is why an effect-size floor is needed with more than an hour of data

justification.dataset: DANDI:000939 is the canonical Peyrache/Duszkiewicz mouse postsubiculum HD-cell dataset, exactly the standard choice for this phenomenon.
justification.handling: Real data streamed via remfile with NaN dropout removal, correct arena/sleep-state epoching, per-unit region and quality metadata, all explicit and defensible.
justification.analysis: Circular statistics, a circular time-shift null, cross-validated Bayesian decoding, and permutation/shuffle controls are all present and correct for the data type.
justification.correctness: Headline numbers reproduce from the committed CSVs, are internally consistent across figures, and the signed decode error tracks the measured rotation session by session.
justification.figures: Every figure is labeled with units and sample sizes, shows both tuned and untuned exemplars, and the effect is unmistakable in tuning curves, decoding, and the moving population bump.
justification.honesty: Claims are proportionate, controls are named, and the write-up openly flags that near-universal significance forces an effect-size floor and that inter-arena rotation is what breaks cross-arena decoding.
justification.verdict: This is a rigorous, correct, and honestly reported multi-session demonstration I would accept as-is.
